en: Jose Rizal wrote the novel Noli Me Tangere to expose the social injustices of the Spanish colonial government in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle is the national bird of the Philippines and is critically endangered due to severe deforestation and illegal hunting.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines is the highest tribunal and holds the judicial branch of the national government.
Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his ancestral home in Kawitan, Cavite.
The Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains over two thousand years ago using simple hand tools.
Fe del Mundo became the first Asian woman admitted to Harvard Medical School and invented a makeshift bamboo incubator.
The sampaguita, a fragrant white jasmine flower, was officially declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
Taal Volcano in Batangas is unique because its main crater lake contains a smaller volcanic island called Volcano Island.
Baybayin is an ancient Philippine writing system that uses carved characters to represent syllables before the Spanish introduced the Latin alphabet.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño with a traditional two-steps forward and one-step backward dance.
Filipino citizens who are at least eighteen years old and properly registered are eligible to vote in national elections.
Filipino painter Juan Luna won a gold medal at the 1884 Madrid Exposition for his famous artwork Spoliarium.
